method: Dense and random IEEE64 numerical validation, together with analytical positive-denominator and forward-rounding bounds; not a machine-checked formal proof. Every original early-break computation unchanged.

real_analysis.series: For 0<x<=1, alternating terms magnitude x^k/(k*k!) and |sum|/x >= 1-1/4. At k=18 the relative term is below double epsilon; cap20 adds margin.
real_analysis.continued_fraction: D_n=b_n-n^2/D_(n-1); C_n=b_n-n^2/C_(n-1); delta_n-1=n^2*(C_(n-1)-D_(n-1))/(C_(n-1)*D_(n-1)*D_n). Equivalently [n^2/(C_(n-1)*D_n)]*(delta_(n-1)-1). For x>=1, positive C,D denominators increase with x, and delta_1-1 decreases, so the slowest exact-real change is at x=1. C_n,D_n >= x+n+1.
real_analysis.b_rounding: Adding integer2 is exact within a binary binade; only binade crossings and initial x+1 round. Geometric sum of crossing ulps is bounded by2*u*bmax. Error propagation conservatively uses4*u*bmax.
floating_point_assumptions: binary64 normal finite arithmetic with per-operation error<=one full ulp (conservative 2u)
no fused multiply-add or unsafe reassociation
positive denominator lower bounds verified; Tiny guards inactive in x>=1
near delta=1 subtraction is exact by Sterbenz lemma
vendor arithmetic and physical timing still require RTL validation
real_analysis.floating_point_scope: The numerical grid is engineering corroboration, not the proof. A sticky numeric_fault bit reports any unexpected exhaustion of either new cap.
